Electric loads on these stages would be reduced versus the base case’s Low and Medium Pressure compression loads – particularly in winter. 4.2 PROCESS ENGINEERING & FLOW DIAGRAM Process engineering has focused on developing a design basis, including assumptions around composition and throughput, followed by development of a robust flow scheme. Simulations were conducted using HYSYS V.14 and the Soave-Redlich-Kwong (SRK) equation of state (EOS). The SRK EOS was selected based on the results of the experimental data collected in the study by H. Li and J. Yan, titled "Evaluating cubic equations of state for calculation of vapor-liquid equilibrium of CO and CO mixtures for CO capture and 2 2 2 Page50 of158 T-RICH Pre-FEED Report – Public Version storage processes." The reliability of five cubic equations of state was assessed in predicting the vapor- liquid equilibrium of CO and binary CO mixtures, which include CH , O , H S, N , Ar, and SO . The results 2 2 4 2 2 2 2 indicate that the SRK equation is superior in calculating the saturated pressure for the vapor-liquid equilibrium properties of CO . The initial phase of work focused on developing a process flow scheme for 2 T-RICH using in-house analogues backed up by simulation to enable sizing and layout of key equipment. 4.2.1 OVERVIEW OF THE PROCESS The T-RICH plant is configured to address the following functional requirements:  Receipt of CO from regional emitters via pipeline, railcars and trucks. 2  Compression, Liquefaction and Inert Removal - to produce a marine transportable liquid CO 2 product  Storage and Tanker Loading This is illustrated in the diagram below. Figure 4.1: Main Process Block Diagram 4.2.2 POTENTIAL CAPACITY IN COMPRESSION AND LIQUEFACTION PROCESS The facility includes an allowance for 7 days of downtime per year. At this stage the preliminary equipment sizing incorporates standard allowances such as:  A 20% allowance for vessel sizing  Conservative assumptions regarding efficiencies when sizing motors and other equipment This approach has allowed the design to progress and support a more efficient design with a low risk of growth in footprint, weight or power consumption. As equipment specifications are finalized, margins can be reduced and replaced by vendor performance guarantees and actual performance data. It is currently anticipated that there is at least a 5% potential increase in throughput, which could translate to an additional 14 days of production capacity. In the next phase of design, the assumption of a 7-day Page51 of158 T-RICH Pre-FEED Report – Public Version shutdown can be revisited to confirm this increased capacity in the design without requiring major changes. During periods of high ambient temperatures, the efficiency of air-cooled heat exchangers decreases as the temperature rises.
